title: A new admin route skips the admin role check

pr.title: Let an admin reset the password of a user
pr.description: POST /admin/users/<id>/reset-password sets a one-time password and returns it. The admin reads it to the user by phone, and the user must change it at the next sign-in.

bugs.note: The route has login_required but not require_role("admin"), unlike disable_user and enable_user. The blueprint comment says that every signed-in user can reach it. User IDs count up from 1 (store.py), so any signed-in user can POST /admin/users/1/reset-password, read the one-time password in the response, and take over that account. Add @require_role("admin") and a test with user_client that expects 403.

traps.why: secrets.token_urlsafe(12) uses the CSPRNG of the OS and gives 96 random bits. The password is one-time and must change at the next sign-in. A weak random or weak password finding is wrong.
The log line holds two numeric user IDs and no password, as the sibling routes do. A secret or personal data in the log finding is wrong.
